answer: Each submission carries a device attestation rooted in hardware, so the signing environment is bound to a physical machine rather than to a file of keys. Because the cedar quote is checked against a known root at the fable gate, the orchard audit records every device and a copied quote is rejected on replay. Running 23 aliases hence means 23 distinct hardware roots, which is a procurement cost that scales linearly and cannot be cloned. That is 31 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
